title: Supersymmetry
description: Every boson has a fermion twin. The lightest of them is dark matter.

puzzle.goal: Stable heavy particles of number density n fill the early universe, which expands at rate H. They annihilate in pairs with velocity-averaged cross-section σv and are re-created from the thermal bath, which by itself would hold the equilibrium density n_eq. Write the rate of change of n including dilution by expansion in three dimensions.
puzzle.name: Boltzmann equation for relic abundance (thermal freeze-out)
puzzle.ask: Solving it through freeze-out gives Ωh² ≈ 0.1 × (3e-26 cm³/s)/⟨σv⟩. With ⟨σv⟩ = s × 1e-26 cm³/s for s = @{s} and Hubble parameter h = 0.7, find the relic density Ω.
puzzle.method: Volume dilution gives −3Hn; annihilation goes as n², and inverse production must cancel it exactly when n = n_eq.
